text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.75 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
This is a public goods game where each token contributed to the group yields 0.75 to each of 4 members, so 3 total versus keeping 1 for myself. Individually it's better to keep, but socially contributing maximizes total payoff, so I'm leaning toward a moderate cooperative contribution rather than full selfishness or full altruism.

I'll contribute 10 as a signal of cooperation without being fully naive about it.

reply.thinking: This is a public goods game where contributing is socially efficient since each token returns 3 total to the group but only 0.75 back to the contributor, while keeping it nets 1 for myself. The dominant individual strategy is to contribute nothing, but full cooperation maximizes collective payoff, so I'm weighing whether to lean selfish or start with a moderate cooperative contribution.

reply.thinking: This is a public goods game where the dominant strategy is to free-ride since contributing only returns 0.75 per token to self while keeping returns 1, yet full group contribution maximizes collective payoff. Given it's a repeated 10-round game with unknown partners, I'm leaning toward a moderate contribution as a balance between self-interest and cooperation.

reply.thinking: Round 1 worked out well with everyone contributing around 10, netting me 40 points. Since others also cooperated at similar levels, I'll keep contributing 10 to sustain that cooperative dynamic into round 2.
